entries.title: The exosome prion chain
entries.claim: Prion-bearing extracellular vesicles transmit disease to animals.
entries.subject: Prions
entries.stage_note: trace complete; 8/8 verified at source. The hypothesis is open, not the trace: the claim as worded depends on vesicle enclosure, which Entry 011 records as untested.
entries.summary: 8-node trace, all verified at source. The pellet transmits; whether the infectivity is inside the vesicles is an open question (Entry 011).
entries.plain_status: Material from the preparation called exosomes causes disease when injected into the brains of PrP-overexpressing mice, in two independent studies. Whether that material is carried inside vesicles, rather than as free aggregate pelleting alongside them, has not been established.

entries.title: The origin of Santa Claus
entries.claim: Santa Claus is a real figure who delivers gifts to children everywhere on one night.
entries.subject: Santa Claus
entries.stage_note: trail mapped; sources not yet verified
entries.summary: Origin trail: St. Nicholas of Myra → Sinterklaas → Moore (1823) → Nast → Coca-Cola. A worked example of tracing a claim to its source — mid-trace.
entries.plain_status: Taken literally — one figure, all children, one night — not supported. The figure's origin is real and datable; that trace is in progress.
entries.author: Priority Nexus LLC

entries.title: Chronic wasting disease and humans
entries.claim: Chronic wasting disease (CWD) can transmit to humans and cause prion disease.
entries.subject: Chronic wasting disease
entries.stage_note: trace complete; all sources verified at source
entries.summary: CWD-to-human transmission. No confirmed human case. Transmission studies conflict across models, isolates and routes.
entries.plain_status: No confirmed human case has been reported. Transmission studies report conflicting results across different models, isolates and routes.

entries.title: The UK appendix prion surveys
entries.claim: Abnormal prion protein found in UK appendix tissue (about 1 in 2,000 people) indicates incubating variant CJD infection.
entries.subject: Variant CJD
entries.stage_note: all five sources read in full at source; stage held at Under Investigation while three citation DOIs, corrected 12 Oct 2026, are re-checked against the nodes they support
entries.summary: UK surveys found abnormal prion protein in ~1 in 2,000 appendixes. Whether that is incubating vCJD is unresolved; the settling experiment is funded but unreported.
entries.plain_status: Abnormal prion protein is present in appendix tissue at about 1 in 2,000. Whether it means incubating vCJD is unresolved: one molecular test leans against it, the direct infectivity test found no transmission from the fixed survey positives, and the amplification test on the positive specimens has not been reported.

entries.title: The autoclave parameters for human prions
entries.claim: The recommended steam-sterilisation parameters (134°C for 18 minutes) inactivate human prions on surgical instruments.
entries.subject: Prion decontamination
entries.stage_note: 3 of 4 sources verified at source; the 1994 decontamination study usually cited for the figure is paywalled (located, not read)
entries.summary: The most-quoted autoclave figure (134°C/18 min) is not tied to a cited inactivation experiment; a single steam cycle leaves residual sporadic-CJD infectivity, while chemical and two-step methods work.
entries.plain_status: The 134°C / 18-minute figure is in the WHO guidance, which cites no inactivation study for it and concedes incomplete removal in worst cases. A readable 2026 bioassay shows a single 134°C cycle does not eliminate one sporadic-CJD strain; chemical and combination treatments do better.
entries.author: Priority Nexus LLC (AI-assisted research; sources checked at publisher 9 Oct 2026)

entries.title: The appendix-assay false-positive rate
entries.claim: The amplification assay proposed to test the UK appendix-survey positives has a measured false-positive rate on known-negative appendix tissue.
entries.subject: Variant CJD
entries.stage_note: key method paper verified at source; the claim is a documented gap, not a positive finding
entries.summary: The assay proposed to test the UK appendix-survey positives has no measured false-positive rate on negative appendix; its validation used a handful of non-CJD controls, not a quantified specificity.
entries.plain_status: The amplification method proposed to test the ~1-in-2,000 appendix positives was validated against a small non-CJD control set that did not amplify. Its specificity — a false-positive rate on known-negative survey-era appendix — has not been quantified, and the assay's substrate is built for one genotype most survey positives do not share.
